title: Wayne J. Crans (1937–2025)
content: It is with deep sadness that we report the passing of the renowned mosquito biologist Wayne John Crans, Ph.D., on 30 July 2025. Our beloved grandfather, father, uncle, teacher, mentor, colleague, and friend passed away peacefully from natural causes in his home after living a completely fulfilled life of 87 years. “Doc,” as he was affectionately called by his family, students, and others, was born in New Jersey on 28 November 1937 and grew up in the New Market area of Piscataway. Wayne loved the outdoors and would take any opportunity to go outside, explore the woods, play in the streets, or go fishing for a welcome adventure. This latter hobby turned him into an avid fly fisherman. He put entomology into practice to master tying his own flies and would eventually teach an Aquatic Entomology for Anglers course at Rutgers University. As an adult, Wayne also spent many hours outdoors hiking, birdwatching, cycling, swimming, snorkeling, and gardening. Wayne’s understanding of and passion for the outdoors was passed on to his three sons, his grandchildren, and many of his students and colleagues.
